# `planet.extremes()` {#fn-planet-extremes}

[Function index](function-index.html#idx-planet-extremes)

```{=html}
<p>An epoch alone does not specify the planet's position in its cycle. The search extends
three quarters of the package's planet-specific period on either side of the epoch,
rounds the limiting years, and samples at daily intervals from noon UT on 1 January of
the start year to the corresponding date in the end year. Each sample uses body.position
and the requested site if supplied. The returned extrema are the range of these samples;
finer extrema can fall between sampled instants.
</p>
<p>Astronomical positions require Swiss Ephemeris files covering the epoch. We
recommend installing <span class="pkg">swephRdata</span>; see <code>skyscapeR-package</code> for setup.
</p>
```

[Illumination and detection](fn-moonphase.qmd).


<details><summary>Implementation arguments, return value and documented modes</summary>

```{=html}
<table><thead><tr><th>Argument</th><th>Formal default</th><th>Behaviour in this interface</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row"><code>obj</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Planet name, with this capitalisation: Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter or Saturn.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>year</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Year for which to do calculations. Historical labels such as <code>"3700 BC"</code> are accepted by <code>astroYear</code>.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>loc</code></th><td><code>NULL</code></td><td><p>This can be either a <em>skyscapeR.horizon</em> object, or a vector with the
latitude, longitude and elevation of the site, in this order.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>epoch</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Earlier argument name for <code>year</code>, retained for existing scripts.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><h5>Return value</h5><p>A list containing planet, min.dec and max.dec. The two declinations are extrema of daily samples and are expressed in degrees.
</p>
```

</details>
